headline: JIBEX opens in Jeddah with a China pavilion and its own visitor counter still reading zero
deck: The building exhibition has named sponsors and exhibitors but has left every headline statistic on its website unfilled, five days from opening.
excerpt: JIBEX opens at Jeddah's exhibition centre on 15 September with Mobedex alongside, a China pavilion and named sponsors — but no published exhibitor, visitor or floor-area figures.
content:
The Jeddah International Building Exhibition opens at the Jeddah Centre for Exhibitions and Events on 15 September, running to 17 September with evening hours of 16:00 to 22:00 and the Mobedex interiors show running concurrently. It is organised by Icon International with KAC.

JIBEX covers building materials, construction equipment and tools, electricity and lighting, safety, security and fire, water technology, waste management, engineering consultancies, and marble, granite and stone. Mobedex takes furniture, paints, doors and windows, hotel equipment, flooring, smart home technology, curtains and home textiles. Participating countries are given as Saudi Arabia, China, Egypt and Jordan.

The sponsor list is real and specific: Saudi Red Bricks holds the diamond position and Petromin Foton silver, with CBGG and Zhejiang as official sponsors of the China pavilion, Reef as co-sponsor and Roznamah as media partner. Named exhibitors include Al-Diyar Al-Mubtakarah, BATCO, Unique Scaffolding, Abwab Aman, SIPOREX, Rose Paints, Marmox, El-Dowegry, Sika, Professional Glass, Diamond Glass and Rock Door.

The China pavilion, with two dedicated sponsors behind it, is the most substantive thing on the roster. Chinese building materials suppliers have been increasing their Saudi presence steadily, and a sponsored national pavilion at a Jeddah show is a distribution play aimed at the western region's contractors rather than a token appearance. SIPOREX, Sika and Marmox on the same list represent the established specification end of the same market.

What the organiser has not published is any number at all. The exhibitor count, visitor count and floor area on its own website render as literal zero-plus placeholders, unfilled five days before the doors open. That is not a minor omission for an exhibition asking suppliers to commit stand budget and contractors to commit time, and it stands in sharp contrast to the dmg cluster running in Riyadh on exactly the same dates, which has published speaker lists, exhibitor rosters and combined attendance projections.

The concurrent Mobedex has a further problem: its own standalone website still advertises April 2025 dates, more than a year stale. Any detail on Mobedex for this edition comes from the JIBEX site rather than from the show's own.

There is also no conference or seminar programme of any kind attached to either exhibition, which limits them to what happens on the floor.

For contractors and specifiers in the western region the show remains worth attending on the strength of its exhibitor list, and Jeddah has fewer building exhibitions competing for that audience than Riyadh does. But an organiser that cannot fill in its own statistics is telling visitors something about how the edition is going.
